claim: In GameNetworkingSockets v1.6.1, a direct-UDP client establishes a connection with a 4-leg exchange that restarts from the first leg every 500 ms: ThinkConnection_ClientConnecting calls SendEndToEndConnectRequest every k_usecConnectRetryInterval (a compile-time constant, 500 ms), which on the UDP transport sends a ChallengeRequest; a ChallengeReply makes the client send one ConnectRequest, and the connection completes on ConnectOK. Losing any of the 4 packets ends that attempt until the next ChallengeRequest. The interval is not a GNS configuration value.
evidence: steamnetworkingsockets_connections.h: const SteamNetworkingMicroseconds k_usecConnectRetryInterval = k_nMillion/2. steamnetworkingsockets_connections.cpp: CSteamNetworkConnectionBase::ThinkConnection_ClientConnecting sends a request when usecNow >= m_usecWhenSentConnectRequest + k_usecConnectRetryInterval and wakes up again at that time. steamnetworkingsockets_udp.cpp: CConnectionTransportUDP::SendEndToEndConnectRequest builds and sends a CMsgSteamSockets_UDP_ChallengeRequest; Received_ChallengeReply builds and sends a CMsgSteamSockets_UDP_ConnectRequest; Received_ConnectOK completes the connection.

sources.location: CConnectionTransportUDP::SendEndToEndConnectRequest (about line 1258), Received_ChallengeReply, Received_ConnectOK (about line 1576) at tag v1.6.1

verification_method: Read-only reading of a fresh shallow clone of tag v1.6.1 (the same commit as F-GNS-001/002), outside the repository; nothing built or run from it.
limitations: Source reading only: the timing under loss is a prediction until EXP-036 measures it. Host-side acceptance needs the application to call AcceptConnection from the status callback, which our transport does inside poll(); that dispatch delay is ours, not GNS's. Duplicated packets (our harsh profile duplicates 5%) were not traced. P2P and relayed paths were not examined.
next_experiment: EXP-036 (predeclared): measure raw GNS establishment under the harsh profile against a Monte Carlo of this 4-leg / 500 ms model, and compare it with the soak's 'establish' phase.
